decisions.reason: The ID Vault was announced as a new feature in 2023 and fits the identity-centric super-app strategy, but it is only a feature with no reported traction, so absorption or removal stays plausible if it falls short of aspiration.

The identity-bound wallet is only mentioned and overlaps with the dedicated payment and wallet framework, so problemistic search could fold it into Product D, though it still supports the payment pillar for now.

The NFC tag authenticator is a niche hardware-dependent add-on with only a passing mention and no evidence of meeting aspirations, which makes it a likely candidate for freeing resources toward the flagship platform in a mid-sized firm with limited slack.
Presented on its own page and central to the payment capability of the super-app ecosystem, the framework appears to meet aspirations and fits core customers in finance and insurance.
As the flagship embodying the firm's strategic direction, the super-app platform receives commitment and slack even under uncertain results, so dropping it is very unlikely.
Application shielding builds directly on the firm's decades of application-security expertise, has a dedicated page, and serves security-sensitive core customers, so it likely meets aspirations.
